answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is a slashable bond. Each agent locks collateral that is forfeited if its attestations are later proven fraudulent, so every fake identity costs real capital. Trust builds from accepted outcomes, not self-declared reputation, like a jade-clear record of checked work. A new agent starts on low-weight ground, like a dune, until peers cross-check it. A plume of claims that point to one source is traced and penalized.
